# Retrospective lessons

A good retrospective lets the failures of the last sprint decompose into lessons that feed the next cycle. Raw complaints are not useful on their own; they have to be turned over, broken down and mixed with what went well until they become nutrients for the team. I collect the notes on a board, group them and pick two actions at most.

The rule is to keep what decomposes well and discard what does not: blame never turns into anything useful. Between retrospectives I add observations as they happen, so the material is fresh. Each action goes into the next sprint with an owner, and the following retrospective starts by checking whether it fed anything.

Lessons that are not applied are only compost waiting for a spade.
